generator.params.crown_height.note: A choice of the model's (woody forms, broadleaf revision 16): the crown's region reaches 13 m, not the species' 21 m maximum, so its umbrella levels out at about 7 m, the height of the grown open trees in iNaturalist photographs (observations 287136128, 135888680). The trunk divides about 2.5 m up (fork_height) under a crown from 3 m (crown_base), and short shoots need 0.3 of the open sky's light (spur_light), so the crown's underside thins as in the photographs.

traits.crown_form.note: iNaturalist research-grade photographs of grown trees (observations 287136128, 135888680, 35563571, 342732647): a short trunk divides low into limbs that spread into a wide, flat-topped crown.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Vachellia tortilis (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.78 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.78, branches 0.69. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tree 4 to 10 m tall of the African savanna and the Arabian and Sinai deserts, whose branches spread from a short trunk into a flat-topped umbrella crown, with paired straight white thorns and short hooked ones, and tiny twice-divided leaves. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.bud_years.note: Short shoots leaf out for up to 40 years while they have light, fitted with the seed plants' shoot spacing so that leaf area per crown area rises with age as the Urban Tree Database's city trees of Vachellia farnesiana (the database's Acacia farnesiana, Glendale, Arizona) does, rather than falling once the crown has filled.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card draws a cluster of its small leaves, a branchlet's worth, 0.26 m long, so that the crown keeps within the module limit; the seed plants' rules space the shoots from the card's area.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 5 m at 20 years and 8 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark bark, white thorns, sparse grey-green leaves. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): grey to black bark, rough and deeply fissured; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: Brenan's manual on Acacia taxonomy for FAO, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): pinnae 2 to 10 pairs (to 14, after Ross 1979) on a rachis up to 2 (4) cm long; leaflets 6 to 20 pairs on each pinna, 0.5 to 2.5 (6) mm long and 0.2 to 1 (1.5) mm wide. Even-pinnate at both levels.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: The leaf drawn as a twice-divided compound leaf (spec rework P4), its pinnae and their leaflets counted from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, a fern's frond stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the pinnae standing out nearly square from a short rachis and their tiny leaflets from them, each leaflet about a third as wide as long, as Brenan's sizes give.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Brenan's Flora of Tropical East Africa account of Mimosoideae (1959, p. 117), as Acacia tortilis: tree 4-21 m high, rarely (probably not in East Africa) a bush 1 m; crown flat or spreading; bark grey to black, fissured; stipules spiny, some short, more or less hooked and to about 5 mm, mixed with long straight whitish ones to about 8(-10) cm; leaf rachis 2 cm or less; pinnae 2-10 pairs, 2-17 mm long; leaflets 6-19 pairs per pinna, usually very small, 0.5-2.5(-6) mm long; flowers cream or whitish, in axillary heads 5-10 mm across on peduncles 4-24 mm; pods contorted or spirally twisted, lengthwise-veined; seeds olive- to red-brown, about 7 mm.
